sources.name: knowledge-items
sources.notes: Portable KIs apply across any project using this framework; project KIs are local to one codebase. KIs pulled from an org knowledge-hub repo carry sync_source (org repo URL) and sync_pulled (ISO date) frontmatter fields. See shared/knowledge/README.md and docs/adrs/ADR-003-enterprise-memory-sync.md.

enterpriseSync.pushFlow: PR only — never direct commit to org repo

sources.name: adrs
sources.owner: adr / badr skills (authoring), memory-engineer (staleness review only — ADRs are a historical record, never edited after the fact)
sources.notes: Answers 'why did we choose X over Y' — never expired or deleted, only superseded by a newer ADR that references it.

sources.name: feature-archive
sources.owner: deliver-feature (writes), memory-engineer (does not curate — this is an immutable historical record, not memory subject to expiration)
sources.notes: Retrieved via context-engineer's bounded-context grep (recency-independent) and analyst's 3-most-recent scan (recency-based) — see docs/runbooks/context-engineering.md section 2.

sources.name: feature-archive-summaries
sources.owner: deliver-feature (writes via summarize-artifact --persist), memory-engineer (does not curate — surrogates are overwritten on re-delivery, not manually edited)
sources.format: markdown with HTML retrieval-surrogate comment header
sources.notes: Written by deliver-feature step 37a after all pipeline artifacts are persisted. These are the files that future BM25/vector retrieval tiers should index first — they contain a ~200-word distillation of the feature's scope and outcome. The HTML comment at the top carries machine-readable metadata (retrieval-surrogate: true, feature, source-artifact, generated, index-first). Lexical search over these surrogates is faster than grepping full artifact sets; vector tiers that land later should build their initial index from these files rather than raw analysis.md files.

sources.name: lessons-learned
sources.owner: extract-lessons (authoring, cross-delivery patterns), promote-memory (authoring, single-delivery triage)
sources.notes: Gated by shared/rules/approval-gates.md — a lesson becoming a rule/prompt change requires explicit human approval.

sources.name: domain-dictionary
sources.owner: analyst (adds new terms), memory-engineer (flags orphaned/unused terms — see scripts/health-check.sh)
sources.notes: Never expired — terms are removed only when the concept they name is fully removed from the codebase.

sources.name: team-topology
sources.notes: Registry entry exists for completeness; this is org-structure data, not a candidate for the promotion/expiration lifecycle.

lexical.description: Tag/domain pre-filter over frontmatter, then full-body LLM judgment read. No embeddings, no vector index — see search-ki's own guardrails for why this is a deliberate choice, not a gap.

lightrag.description: Optional future retrieval backend. Markdown remains canonical regardless of status — any LightRAG result must be verified against its source markdown file before being trusted. See docs/runbooks/lightrag-integration.md for when and how to enable this; not built yet because no source in this registry has outgrown lexical search.
